description: A procurement lead must decide whether to authorize a rented robotic palletizer for a peak-season packaging run and finalize the installation, anchoring, validation, and staffing controls, with input from maintenance, safety, quality, and production training.

shared_context.S1: A rental robotic palletizer is available for installation in Bay 7 before next week's peak-season packaging run.
shared_context.S2: Bay 7 has adequate access for delivery, and the rental quotation covers the palletizer, installation support, and operator training.
shared_context.S3: Elena has authority to approve the rental and set the conditions for deploying the equipment.
shared_context.S4: The plant's normal pre-deployment review includes a roundtable in which maintenance, safety, quality, and production training report relevant requirements before procurement approval.

PF1.text: Ravi confirmed with the rental technician this week that the palletizer requires a 6-hour electrical tie-in and a 2-hour dry-run before production; the technician's email has not yet been attached to the rental work order.

PF2.text: Marta's floor-load review found that Bay 7 may be used only with two 1.2-meter steel anchor plates under the palletizer feet and a 3-meter marked exclusion zone; she completed the review from the latest structural drawing, but the installation packet still shows the old unanchored layout.

PF3.text: Jonah confirmed in the customer's packaging protocol that the first 120 cases palletized by a new cell must receive barcode scan verification before normal release; he received the protocol from the customer this week but has not added it to the quality checklist.

PF4.text: Tessa's training-roster audit shows that exactly 3 employees currently hold the palletizer certification required for production, so all three must be assigned to the run and no uncertified substitute may operate the cell; the audit was completed yesterday and the roster board has not been updated.

acceptance_conditions: The rental palletizer must be authorized for the peak-season run.
Installation must include exactly 6 hours of electrical tie-in downtime and a 2-hour dry-run.
The palletizer must use two 1.2-meter steel anchor plates and maintain a 3-meter exclusion zone.
Barcode scan verification must cover exactly the first 120 cases before normal release.
Exactly 3 certified operators must be assigned, and uncertified operation must not be allowed.
The settlement must record commitments for the installation and dry-run, safety setup, barcode verification, and certified staffing.

decisive_facts.why: The rental technician's confirmed requirements change installation downtime to exactly 6 hours, add exactly 2 hours of dry-run time, and require the electrical-tie-in-and-dry-run commitment.
The structural review changes the setup from an unanchored placement to two 1.2-meter anchor plates with a 3-meter exclusion zone and requires the anchoring-and-exclusion-zone commitment.
The customer protocol changes startup quality control to barcode verification on exactly the first 120 cases and requires the barcode-first-article-verification commitment.
The training audit changes staffing to exactly 3 certified operators, prohibits uncertified operation, and requires the certified-operator-assignment commitment.
